title: Effectiveness of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) with Batfish for LLM-generated vendor CLI configurations — preregistered design (repaired)
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses an LLM for config generation, Batfish as a deterministic verifier plus a secondary automated checker, and an automated LLM-based repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic/safety failures compared to plain LLM generation for vendor-specific network configuration tasks?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR pipeline (LLM generation + Batfish verification + automated repair loop) yields a higher paired success rate (proportion of tasks passing verifier checks after GVR) than direct LLM outputs (paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline > 0).

H2: For the planned task set, the median number of automated repair iterations required to reach a Batfish pass is < 5 and the median end-to-end (generation→verification→repair→final-verify) latency per task remains within the preregistered operational bound (median ≤ 60 s).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do failure-mode reductions (syntax vs semantic vs reachability) distribute across vendor families (Cisco-like vs Juniper-like)?
EQ2: How sensitive are paired outcomes to prompt perturbations (published frozen prompt ± small controlled perturbations)?
EQ3: What fraction of tasks are flagged as potentially contaminated by provenance overlap with public corpora (contamination sensitivity analysis)?
benchmark_scope: Public NetConfEval-style intent→CLI tasks (publicly available examples) plus deterministic synthetic task generator for coverage gaps
Two vendor-CLI families: Cisco-like and Juniper-like (synthetic dialects derived from public vendor docs)
Synthetic topologies (deterministically seeded) representative of small-to-medium enterprise networks (10–50 devices) generated by the published topology generator
model_scope: Hosted LLM API (single model identifier frozen for confirmatory runs; model_id documented below)
LLM used only for generation and repair prompts; verifiers and analyzers are deterministic, local/CPU-executable tools
transformation_scope: Deterministic CLI normalization (whitespace, canonical ordering where safe) and token-level sanitization
Automated diffing to compute config deltas
Automated mapping from verifier counterexample to structured repair prompt (template-based)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design with N=300 independent intents (task pairs). Tasks are generated deterministically from: (a) public NetConfEval-style examples (≥150 items) and (b) synthetic generator seeded RNG (≥150 items) to reach 300 total. Two vendor clusters: Cisco-like (150 tasks) and Juniper-like (150 tasks). Each intent yields one baseline LLM output and one GVR pipeline execution (GVR includes initial generation plus repair iterations). Task cluster count = 2 (vendors). All seeds, generator code, and dataset provenance will be published. Inclusion: public-sourceable tasks or synthetic tasks generated by the published generator. Exclusion: tasks whose intended semantics cannot be represented in the synthetic topologies; deterministic exclusion rules implemented in code and logged. Confirmatory items (pair count) = 300. Derivation: 2 vendors × 150 tasks/vendor = 300 pairs.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by the registered 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor. Primary analysis: paired test of verifier pass-rate difference (GVR final pass vs baseline initial pass) using the executor's McNemar/paired-proportion method, estimator 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Failed-call treatment (primary): 'complete_pair_primary' (pairs with genuine infrastructure/model API failures are excluded only if both methods failed due to technical issues; see missingness_plan). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' where failed LLM calls are treated as failures (zero) to produce conservative bounds. Report 95% CIs and exact paired p-values. Secondary analyses: Wilcoxon signed-rank for latency and median repair iterations; stratified analyses by vendor and failure-mode. Multiplicity-adjusted secondary comparisons use Bonferroni correction across at most 3 secondary estimands.
multiplicity_plan: Primary estimand (paired success-rate difference) is pre-specified and tested at α=0.05. Secondary estimands (median iterations, median latency, failure-mode stratified differences) are reported with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds (α_adjusted = 0.05 / number_of_secondary_tests) for any formal hypothesis tests. Exploratory analyses are labeled as such and not used to support primary claims.
missingness_plan: Technical LLM/API failures and verifier crashes are logged with deterministic failure codes. Primary treatment: pairs where model generation for either condition fails due to transient infrastructure errors will be retried up to the preregistered retry policy (max 2 automatic retries per failed call); if retries exhausted, the pair is handled according to 'complete_pair_primary' (excluded from primary test only if exclusionary failure provenance indicates infrastructure error that equally affected both arms). Sensitivity analysis treats any missing model output as a negative (failure) in 'failure_as_zero' modality. All exclusions and retry attempts are fully logged and hashed for reproducibility.

risk_factors: Training-data overlap between the hosted LLM and public NetConf examples
Synthetic generator producing items identical to public corpus examples
detection_procedures: Provenance cross-check: exact-string and fuzzy-match against publicly indexed corpora (public URLs/DOIs) to flag near-duplicates
Automated n-gram overlap score and heuristics to flag likely contamination (thresholds preregistered)
Secondary check: for flagged items, run alternate prompts (perturbation) and compare outputs for overfitting signals
item_flagging_rules: If exact match to a public example → flag as 'duplicate_public' and exclude from primary confirmatory analysis (will be retained only in exploratory contamination-rate reports)
If fuzzy-match overlap > preregistered threshold → flag as 'likely_overlap' and included in sensitivity analyses only
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes exact-public-duplicates. Sensitivity analyses report results (a) including flagged items, and (b) treating flagged items as separate subgroup to quantify contamination effect.
residual_uncertainty: Remaining probability that hosted LLM memorized unseen public configs but does not produce identical outputs (undetectable contamination)
Coverage gaps in public corpora indexing leading to false negatives in detection

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal confirmatory run to conserve model-call budget while still performing paired test: N=150 pairs (75 per vendor).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-pair planned LLM calls: baseline generation (1) + GVR initial generation (1) + expected median repair iterations (2) = 4 calls/pair. 4 × 150 = 600 calls. Within capability manifest model-call ceiling and practical for a short run; reduced power relative to recommended scenario.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended confirmatory run balanced for power and budget: N=300 pairs (150 per vendor).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-pair planned LLM calls: baseline (1) + GVR initial (1) + expected median repairs (2) = 4 calls/pair → 4 × 300 = 1200 planned calls. This is within the selected candidate's estimated_model_calls (1500) and the capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10000). Chosen as recommended to reach target power for a modest (~10 percentage-point) paired difference detection.

power_plan.target_effect: Detect a 0.10 absolute increase in pass-rate (e.g., from 0.40 baseline to 0.50 after GVR) with 80% power at α=0.05 (two-sided) using paired-proportion test assumptions.
power_plan.clustering_unit: per-intent paired observation (one baseline output and one GVR final outcome per task)
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate McNemar/pairwise sample-size approximation (normal approximation for difference in paired proportions); conservative target N≈300 pairs chosen after sensitivity analysis across baseline pass-rate scenarios (0.30–0.50) and effect sizes (0.08–0.12).
assumptions: Baseline verifier pass-rate between 0.30 and 0.50 (based on domain literature and pilot checks on public examples).
Correlation of paired outcomes approximated via discordant-pair rates consistent with a 0.10 absolute effect.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=300 pairs and baseline 0.40 pass-rate, power to detect ≈10 percentage-point absolute change ≈80%. If baseline pass-rate is lower (0.30) or higher (0.50), detectable effect size for same power shifts by ±~2–3 percentage points; sensitivity analyses will report exact achieved power via bootstrap.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute achieved power under baseline pass-rates of 0.30, 0.40, 0.50 and effect sizes 0.08–0.12 via bootstrap on observed discordant-pair rates.
Repeat power calculation for the minimal scenario (N=150) to report reduced sensitivity.

transformation_families: Config diff and semantic delta computation
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated Batfish reachability and policy checks before/after normalization to confirm semantics preserved by normalization where applicable
Round-trip parser check: parse(normalize(generated_config)) == normalize(parse(generated_config)) for deterministic grammar-covered constructs
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject (auto-fail the pair) if generated config fails syntax parsing by vendor grammar parser (deterministic)
Detect identical repeated outputs across repair iterations (hash equality) and automatically stop repair loop (oscillation detection)
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Deterministic 10% stratified audit (by vendor and initial-fail vs initial-pass) using additional automated analyzers (syntax parser + independent static-check scripts). Audit selection deterministic via seeded RNG; all audit artifacts logged and hashed.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Repair-prompt templates validated by unit tests ensuring required fields (counterexample excerpt, failing-rule id, topology snippet) are consistently present. All transformation code and templates published with deterministic tests.
residual_risks: Incomplete vendor grammar coverage may mis-classify some syntax-valid configs as syntax failures (false positives).
Normalization may alter intent in corner cases not covered by semantic-equivalence checks.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Residual verifier false negatives: Batfish + secondary automated checks reduce but do not eliminate the possibility that some semantic violations go undetected; this affects external validity but not the paired comparison internal validity bounded to verifier-detected failures.

Public dataset vendor-coverage: synthetic generator mitigates but cannot fully replicate production vendor subtle constructs; generalization to production-grade vendor dialects is noncritical to internal confirmatory claims but limits external generality.
Hosted LLM nondeterminism and provider training-corpus overlap: contamination-detection reduces risk but cannot prove absence of memorization signatures for all tasks.
